items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I'm not that familiar with Stuff Smith. I'd be the first to admit it, you know, I'm not saying… he's a wonderful musician, but I'm not familiar with his music the same way I was with the bebop, you know, Charlie Parker.

ctx.x: Well, Don Cherry is born the same day as I am, except there was ten years difference in our… I‟m ten years older than him. And um, I‟m… I don‟t remember how I met Don. I don‟t remember how I met him. But I know that Cameron‟s always been after me to write lyrics to like, uh, Don, you know. Well, Don Cherry got me… he was still alive when I wrote lyrics. No, I didn‟t write lyrics. He was still alive when he asked me to write some lyrics for Art Deco. „Cause that‟s one more one, one of his compositions that‟s a…
spirit. He was, he‟s another, he‟s another gem. Gem of a musician and as a human being. Just absolutely beautiful. So… Don Cherry.
